name: competitors
title: Competition
description: Every competitor mention, with the buyer's actual relationship to it and — when the buyer says it — the quote naming why they'd switch. An active user and someone migrating away are opposite signals; the schema keeps them separate.
prompt:
List every mention of a competing product or vendor — one entry per mention. A generic reference to "other tools" with no identifiable product is not a competitor mention. An empty list is correct when none came up.

For each mention:
- evidence: cite the utterance(s), before you write "text". The line that establishes the relationship value below must be among the quotes you cite here — the label rides on it.
- text: the mention in the speaker's exact words — no digit/number-word conversion, no paraphrase.
- competitor: the competitor's name exactly as spoken (lowercase if the transcript is lowercase). Never normalize to an official brand spelling the transcript does not contain.
- relationship: the buyer's actual relationship, judged by an observable cue in the quote. active_user = present-tense usage today ("we use X", "we're on X"); migrating_from = language of leaving ("moving off X", "replacing X", "X isn't working"); evaluating = considering it now ("we're also looking at X", "demoing X"); mentioned = named with no stated relationship. When the cue is not clearly one of these, use "mentioned" rather than guessing a stronger signal.
- switching_trigger: ONLY when the buyer states a reason they would leave (or joined) that competitor, capture it as its own receipt — evidence (the utterance) then text (the buyer's exact words, e.g. "their support is terrible"). Use null when the buyer names no such reason. Do not infer a trigger from tone.

Do not classify the competitor as direct/adjacent and do not rate the buyer's sentiment — those are not reliably readable from a single transcript and this extractor does not emit them. Report only what a quote supports.
